title: Fixation Hold with Peripheral Flash
summary: A fixation-hold task with a brief peripheral flash on half the trials; measure whether fixation survives the flash.
paradigm: Each trial begins by requiring the subject to acquire fixation within a timeout. Once fixation is acquired, the subject must hold fixation for a set duration. On half the trials, a brief peripheral flash stimulus appears during the fixation hold period; on the other half, no flash is presented. The trial measures whether fixation is maintained through the flash or not. Conditions differ by presence or absence of the flash and are served equally according to the scheduler. Trials that do not complete (e.g., fixation breaks) are repeated rather than counted.

design.label: Expected session length
design.value: about 10 minutes, depending on subject response times and breaks

Continue holding fixation after flash until hold duration completes
Mark trial outcome based on fixation hold success

tasks.description: A task where the subject fixates a central point and holds fixation. On half the trials, a brief peripheral flash is presented during the hold. The trial measures whether fixation is maintained through the flash.
tasks.name: fixation-flash-hold

notes: Flash duration and eccentricity chosen as conventional values; flash size and luminance not specified and left to implementation. Flash occurs midway through the hold fixation period. Flash is presented peripherally at 8 dva eccentricity on the right side. Half the trials have the flash, half do not.
